disease_label_per_paper: Muckle-Wells syndrome within the cryopyrin-associated periodic syndrome spectrum
presentation_summary: 3-year-old Chinese boy referred in 2020 with recurrent fever without apparent cause for more than 10 months.
Each fever episode generally lasted 1-5 days, with an interval of approximately 15 days between episodes; temperature was usually about 37.5 C with occasional blips up to 39 C.
During fever episodes he had bilateral conjunctival congestion and urticarial-like rash.
The report states there was no fatigue, headache, nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, sore throat, cough, asthma, abdominal pain, vomiting, diarrhea, or joint swelling/pain.
Routine blood examination showed elevated leukocyte count, neutrophil count, ESR, CRP, and SAA.
NLRP3 c.784-786delinsTGG p.R262W, parental negative testing, final paper diagnosis, and thalidomide response are preserved as confirmatory/non-ranking context.

actual_treatment.source_text_value: oral thalidomide at 12.5 mg, twice a day

outcome.clinical_course: Symptoms were controlled during thalidomide treatment; the paper recommended long-term follow-up for hearing damage, AA amyloidosis, and kidney damage.

quality_warnings: Genetic sequencing, final diagnosis, de novo inheritance confirmation, and thalidomide response are confirmatory/non-ranking.
The paper reports elevated inflammatory markers without exact numeric values; this is encoded through a composite acute-phase activity axis rather than invented labs.
